rubrics.criterion: In the A* engine, the per-search bookkeeping that the traversal, relaxation, and between-search reset steps shared is owned by a single abstraction, so no internal engine signature still receives the whole bookkeeping group as separate parameters.
rubrics.rationale: The engine's bookkeeping (open/closed tracking plus the node registry) was the largest recurring group injected into this case; resolving it is the core obligation for the astar component.

rubrics.criterion: In the grid world and its image export, the world-plus-position threading is gone: the bounds/open checks, the obstacle-shadow corner checks, and the per-cell paint step no longer each receive the world and its coordinates as separate parameters, and the state or values they need are reached through the re-owned abstraction.
rubrics.rationale: This cluster spans three files (world, node traversal, generator) and both the navigation and rendering execution paths; resolving it is the core obligation for the grids component.

rubrics.criterion: In the word breaker, the shared parse state (dictionary set and memo) has one owner, so the recursion no longer re-receives dictionary, memo, and input together as a piecemeal parameter list; the input being parsed at each level remains a genuine per-call argument rather than being absorbed into the shared state.
rubrics.rationale: This case deliberately hides a boundary decision inside the word-breaker cluster: input rides alongside the shared state in the injected signatures but is a per-level value. A repair that bundles input into the shared state has not resolved the group correctly.

rubrics.criterion: In the moving-average statistics, the sliding-window bookkeeping (running sum, window capacity, element queue) is owned by a single abstraction, so the window append, eviction, and average-read helpers no longer take those members as separate parameters.
rubrics.rationale: The window cluster is the fourth injected group and its members are tied to the owner by mutation (the sum is threaded by pointer); resolving it completes the required scope.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not widen any group beyond its real boundary: genuine per-call values (the string being parsed in the word breaker, the number appended in the moving average, the neighbor node examined by the grid corner checks) are not absorbed into the shared owners, and unrelated independent values (such as the image writer's one-off setup list) are not collapsed into any new owner.
rubrics.rationale: Over-grouping is the characteristic failure mode when removing data clumps in this codebase: the surrounding code contains lookalike parameter lists that the required outcome explicitly excludes.

rubrics.criterion: Every internal call site of the formerly threaded helpers was rewired to the new owners, including the public delegating methods of each component; no call site still passes the old member list, repacks it into the old shapes, or forwards through a leftover intermediate.
rubrics.rationale: The injected pattern lives at the call sites as much as in the signatures; a repair that only re-homes the extracted helpers but leaves caller-side member lists (e.g. grid traversal still computing and passing coordinates one by one to loose functions, or delegating methods still unpacking their fields) has not finished the change.

rubrics.criterion: Per-call derived values are handled at the right place in the new design: the neighbor coordinates derived during the grid traversal and the obstacle-shadow corner logic consume the moving node's position and the neighbor through the re-owned abstraction rather than re-threading a world pointer with each derived pair.
rubrics.rationale: In this case the recurring group's coordinates are derived at each call site from the moving node and loop counters, so the repair must decide where derivation belongs relative to the new owner — the main coordination decision beyond re-homing the state.

rubrics.criterion: The word breaker's recently extracted dictionary/memo probe operates within the re-owned parsing abstraction rather than remaining a loose function that receives the whole parse state from outside.
rubrics.rationale: The probe was the last helper added by the sweep and exists only to serve the word breaker's recursion; whether it is kept, folded in, or re-shaped, it belongs inside the parsing responsibility once the state is owned.

rubrics.criterion: The finished change leaves no internal scaffolding whose only purpose was to forward or repack the previously threaded members: no unused or orphaned helper, no leftover signature kept just to hold the member list, and no duplicate path that exists only to avoid rewiring one caller.
rubrics.rationale: This case's injection added helper indirection in four packages; a partial cleanup that re-owns the state but keeps the now-redundant threading helpers or delegations behind leaves the sweep's residue in place.

rubrics.criterion: No public constructor or method signature changed: the A* engine's public entry points, the grid world's constructors, accessors, and the demo helper its test calls directly, the word breaker's public functions, and the moving average's public methods keep their exact names, signatures, and return types.
rubrics.rationale: The task freezes the public surface by design (the public API and the directly-called grid demo helper are the downstream consumers' contract), so signature drift is a concrete, easily observed failure.

rubrics.criterion: Observable behavior is unchanged: diagonal moves are still rejected exactly under the obstacle-corner rules, word splits and word extractions return the same results, moving-average eviction order and arithmetic are identical, and the rendered image content is identical.
rubrics.rationale: The four changed behaviors (neighbor filtering, word parsing, window arithmetic, image painting) are the observable outputs of this repository's tests and demos; each is a place where a careless re-ownership could silently change results.

rubrics.criterion: A search instance reused across consecutive searches behaves like a fresh instance: no open entries, visited entries, or node wrappers leak from one search into the next because the reset the engine performs clears the state the instance actually holds.
rubrics.rationale: The engine's bookkeeping lives longer than one query in this codebase, and the injected reset mutates the shared structures in place; a repair that resets a copy, or that moves bookkeeping into per-search locals without clearing what the instance retains, reintroduces or hides state-leak bugs.
